    StartersAlley nachosLeague night with Walter and DonnyHow to make it1 onion, diced1 tbsp vegetable oil1 green chilli, diced1 tsp ground cumin1 tomato, diced375ml evaporated milk200g cheddar, grated250g corn chips40g pickled jalapenos150g sour cream1 small bunch corianderCook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes.Add the chilli, cumin and tomato and cook 3 minutes.Add the evaporated milk and bring to a simmer, then take off the heat and stir in the cheddar until smooth.Divide the corn chips between 4 cardboard trays, pour over the queso and top with jalapenos, sour cream and coriander. Serve straight away.Rug-pattern paprika lavash crackersMind the rugHow to make it2 lavash sheets3 tbsp olive oil1/2 tsp smoked paprika1/2 tsp ground cumin10g sesame seeds150g feta100g Greek yoghurt1 lemon, zestedCut the lavash into 12 rectangles and brush with some of the oil.Sprinkle with paprika, cumin and sesame seeds in alternating stripes.Bake at 180°C until crisp, then cool.Blitz the feta, yoghurt, lemon zest and remaining oil until smooth for dipping.Half-and-half whipped ricotta honey dipThe Dude buys it in his dressing gownHow to make it300g ricotta100g cream cheese2 tbsp creamsalt, to taste1 lemon, zested3 tbsp honey1/2 tsp chilli flakes1 sourdough loaf2 tbsp olive oilcracked black pepper, to tasteBeat the ricotta, cream cheese and cream with a pinch of salt and the lemon zest until very smooth, about 2 minutes.Warm the honey with the chilli flakes in a small pan.Slice the sourdough loaf into fingers, brush with olive oil and grill or toast 2 minutes a side.Spread the ricotta in a shallow bowl, drizzle with the hot honey and finish with plenty of cracked black pepper. Serve with the sourdough.MainsAlley burgersWalter, Donny and the Dude between framesHow to make it600g potatoesneutral oil, for frying1 tsp salt700g beef mince120g American-style cheese4 burger buns60g mayonnaise20g tomato sauce10g mustard1 onion, thinly sliced80g dill picklesCut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry thoroughly.Blanch in oil at 140°C for 5 minutes, drain and cool 15 minutes.Fry again at 185°C until crisp and season with salt.Smash 8 loose balls of mince thin on a hot griddle and season.Cook 2 minutes a side, melting the cheese on top.Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce and mustard. Fill the toasted buns with two patties, onion, pickles and sauce. Chips on the side.Drive-thru burgerEaten in the Dude's beat-up carHow to make it400g beef mince2 onions, diced2 tsp chilli powder1 tsp ground cumin400g tinned tomatoes400g tinned kidney beans, drained8 beef franks8 hot dog buns100g cheddar, grated3 tbsp American mustardBrown the beef mince with 1 diced onion in a large pan.Add the chilli powder, cumin, tomatoes and kidney beans and simmer 25 minutes until thick.Simmer the beef franks for 5 minutes, then sear on a hot griddle until blistered.Toast the hot dog buns.Fill each bun with a frank and chilli, then the cheddar, the rest of the onion and mustard.SweetsCoffee liqueur ice cream cookie sandwichesFor the half and halfHow to make it150g butter200g brown sugar1 egg250g plain flour1/2 tsp bicarb soda150g choc chips1 L vanilla ice cream60ml coffee liqueur50g chocolate-coated coffee beans, crushedBrown the butter, cool, then beat with the sugar and egg.Mix in the flour, bicarb soda and choc chips.Chill the dough overnight (included in cook time).Bake 16 small balls at 180°C until golden and cool.Soften the ice cream and ripple through the coffee liqueur.Refreeze for 1 hour.Sandwich scoops between the cookies and roll the edges in the crushed coffee beans.Freeze for 30 minutes before serving.DrinksWhite RussianThe Dude's drink, every sceneHow to make it400g ice180ml vodka80ml coffee liqueur120ml thickened creamDivide the ice among four rocks glasses and add 45ml vodka and 20ml coffee liqueur to each.Top each with 30ml thickened cream and stir lazily.
